newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia says working hard on energy firm sale.
newsitem.headline: Latvia says working hard on energy firm sale.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday it was working hard on the privatisation of the Latvenergo monopoly energy supplier and hopes to complete another stage of the process with a final audit next year.
Offers have already been invited for around 25 percent to 35 percent of Latvenergo and companies such as Preussen, Watenfall and Finnish Voima have expressed an interest.

"Serious work has begun in preparing Latvenergo for privatisation after the Privatisation Agency signed an agreement with the EBRD," Andrejs Tiknuss, privatisation department head, told a news conference.
The deal with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) provides for an analysis of the best ways to recapitalise the company and for an audit by May 31 next year.
The recapitalisation analysis will be carried out by Deutsche Bank and the audit by Deloitte and Touche.
Latvenergo made a profit of 9.03 million lats in 1995 but owes millions of dollars to energy suppliers.
Stakes in monopoly gas supplier Latvian Gas have already been sold to Gazprom and a Ruhrgas/Preussen consortium.
